title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and began with a public hearing to discuss the Community Development Block Grant Program.  The $1.5 Million grant was awarded to the City of Flora to reline sanitary sewer lines, line manholes and related costs in a targeted area and the work is essentially complete with the final clean up this spring.  It was issued by the federal government and administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity.  The hearing’s purpose was to give the public a chance to speak out on the project.  With no public comment, the hearing adjourned.

Mayor Linda Spicer then called the regular meeting to order and asked for public comments.  Haley Coble with Flora American Legion Post #14 Auxiliary addressed commissioners with a request to use Charley Brown Park for an Easter Egg Hunt on Saturday, April 4 at 1:00pm.  Coble explained that Legion seeks to put on a family friendly event that is free in age specific hunts.  She and the group are committed to putting on the event to strengthen community spirit and pledged to follow any requirements the city puts forward.  Commissioners quickly approved their request.

The council then voted to approve the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included approval of past meeting minutes, the warrant list for February as well as approval of a permit for the placement of a mausoleum at Elmwood Cemetery.

In regular business, Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger asked for commissioners to approve the purchase and training of a narcotics canine from Vohne Liche Kennels in Denver, Indiana.  The cost is $21,477 that also includes the training of Flora Police Officer Luke Durre.  The current narcotics canine is being retired after several years on the job.  The measure was approved unanimously.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford introduced Lee Beckman with Milano and Grunloh Engineers from Effingham with an update on grant applications for the city.  Beckman stated that the city is applying for $1.9 Million in grant funding for water main upgrades through IEPA.  The grant application is due each year by March 31, so Flora’s application will not be submitted until March of 2027 with the expectation that the work would be completed by 2029.  Mike Stanford asked commissioners to approve an ordinance ratifying a façade improvement grant for Charm Hair Company LLC at 402 W. North Avenue in the amount of $2,395 for lighting and signage.  Commissioners approved the request without dissent.  Members also approved an ordinance for the purchase of 103 Rio Grande behind the hub, from Donnie and Joni Pollard in the amount of $30,000.

Flora City Clerk Kaci O’Dell asked commissioners to approve closed session minutes from February 17, 2026 and members did as she requested.  And with all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: IECC MOBILIZES
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges is mobilizing campus and community resources to support workers and families impacted by the sudden closure of Champion Laboratories in Albion.

IECC is coordinating training opportunities, financial assistance and career services to assist the more than 1,000 affected employees during this uncertain time.

“For many, this is a deeply difficult moment, and I believe it is a moment where IECC needs to step forward to lend assistance,” said IECC Chancellor Dr. Ryan Gower.  “We are not simply a collection of campuses and programs.  We are part of the economic infrastructure of this region.  When a major employer closes, we have a responsibility to step in and assist.”

A series of informational workshops have been scheduled to help employees of Champion Labs learn about services available under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.  These sessions will provide clear guidance on unemployment benefits, health insurance coverage, 401K and retirement benefits, utility assistance and training and education opportunities.

Presenters include the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, Southern 14 Workforce Investment Board, Illinois Eastern Community Colleges, US Department of Labor/Employee Benefits Security Administration, and the Illinois Department of Employment Security.

Meetings will be held in the Workforce Building at Frontier Community College on the following dates on Thursday, at 10 am for people whose last names beginning with A-E.  Then at 1:30 pm for those whose last names beginning with F-J.

Then on Friday, at 10 am for those whose last names beginning with K-O, and at 1:30 pm for those whose last names beginning with P-T.  Then on Monday, March 9 at 10 am for those whose last names beginning with U-Z, and at 1:30 pm for anyone who was unable to attend a previous session.

IECC staff and workforce partners will be available to answer questions and help individuals as they move forward.  Those unable to attend are encouraged to schedule a one-on-one appointment with an advisor at any IECC campus.

In addition, IECC is developing fast-track training options designed to help displaced workers return to the workforce as quickly as possible.  These opportunities in industrial and manufacturing technology, logistics and healthcare entry roles offer completion times ranging from just a few days to one semester.

Detailed information regarding training options and financial assistance will be provided during the meetings.  Additional information and resources are available on the IECC website at www.iecc.edu/championlabs.

Dr. Sharmila Kakac, FCC President and IECC Vice Chancellor of Business and Industry, encourages affected employees to participate in the upcoming meetings and to take full advantage of the many resources available.

“No one should feel they have to navigate this transition alone,” she said.  “IECC and our workforce partners stand ready to provide personalized, one-on-one assistance.  Whether someone needs immediate employment support or is considering new training or credentials, we are here to help them move forward with confidence.  Taking that first step can open doors to opportunities many may not have previously considered.”

title: BLOOD SHORTAGE
full_story:
In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have a blood drive on Monday, March 9th at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm.  By donating at this drive you can help one or more graduating seniors earn a scholarship.  Each student who recruits one presenting donor will receive a Red Cross plush pillow.  Donors will also receive a $15 Amazon Gift Card by email.

The Red Cross is asking healthy individuals to book an appointment to give blood or platelets by using the Blood Donor App, visiting RedCrossBlood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS.  The donation process can be streamlined by completing the Rapid Pass health history also online at RedCrossBlood.org/rapidpass.  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

There will also be an Impactlife blood drive on Thursday, March 12th at the Clay County Hospital from 9:30 to 12:30 pm.

title: 2,500 VALENTINES SENT
full_story:
In an effort to brighten the lives of senior citizens across the Metro East and Southern Illinois, nearly 2,500 Valentine’s Day cards were collected through State Senator Jason Plummer’s annual Valentine’s Day program and shared with residents at long-term care facilities throughout the 55th Senate District.

The cards were collected from local schools, churches, community groups, and residents throughout the district and distributed to several facilities to help bring joy to seniors during the Valentine’s Day season.

“Our seniors are an important part of our communities, and this program is a meaningful way to come together and show how much they are appreciated,” said Sen. Plummer.  “I’m thankful to everyone who took the time to make or send a card this year.”

This year’s program marked the sixth year Sen. Plummer has hosted the Valentine’s Day card drive for seniors across the 55th Senate District.  Since the program began in 2021, Sen. Plummer has collected more than 14,000 valentines for seniors throughout the district.

title: CO2 EXPOSURE
full_story:
Health officials in Illinois released the results of new research highlighting the dangers of carbon monoxide.

According to the Illinois Department of Health and Human Services, the first-of-its-kind report looked at carbon monoxide exposures between 2019 and 2023.  During that time period, they say exposures lead to an average of 940 trips to the emergency room, 126 hospitalizations and 57 deaths every year in Illinois.

The research found carbon monoxide exposures are most common between October and March, but officials say they can happen at any time of the year.  IDPH plans to use the findings to improve awareness and prevention of carbon monoxide exposures.

title: SPRING OUTLOOK
full_story:
Illinois State Climatologist Trent Ford was ask what’s in store for the spring weather outlook in Illinois—March through May?

Ford says most of Illinois is playing catch-up in the moisture game.  Drought impacts haven’t changed much this winter with concern growing in east central Illinois where D3 or extreme drought status is in play.
